title: MedlinePlus says infant movement starts at the head and moves downward
summary: MedlinePlus says an infant's physical development begins at the head and then moves to other parts of the body.
body: MedlinePlus says physical development begins at the head, then moves to other parts of the body. The example on the page puts sucking first, a sit next, and getting around on the feet after that. The sentence is an order, not a month. CDC ages for separate skills are other cards. This card is only that head-first order. It is one encyclopedia's description, not a timetable for one infant.

sources.title: Infant - newborn development
sources.author: MedlinePlus
sources.note: Opening physical-development sentence: development begins at the head, then moves to other parts of the body, with sucking before sitting before walking.
